items.title: Interview | Calum Paterson
items.text: Callum, thank you for joining us as you approach a year in the job as heart of Medlovian chairman. Just firstly, how are things? All all good? Yeah, all good, thank you. And yeah, coming up for a year, which is enough time for me to realize how allconsuming football can be. Uh, but it's a privilege for me to be involved and I'm really enjoying the role. Take you back 12 months then. What were some of the things that made you want to take the role on? Uh well first and foremost because Harts is my team. I've been a supporter from a young age when I was growing up in Lithco. I've also been a member of the foundation of hearts from its early days. So when the opportunity to get involved came up. I felt that my experience could perhaps be of some use to the club. Uh my business career has mainly been uh as an investor in growing companies working closely with their management teams and boards through periods of of change and transformation. So hopefully relevant. But of course I came into the role knowing that I had a lot to learn uh because football's different uh as I'm regularly reminded and there's certainly no shortage of of opinions in football. But uh ultimately I felt it was an opportunity for me to give something back and to play a part in helping the club progress. Uh I'm also genuinely excited about the opportunity that lies ahead for Harts and we're really fortunate to have some outstanding people backing the club on its on its journey. What does success for Heart of Mlovian look like to you then? Well, we're aiming high. Uh we want hearts to be competitive at the top end of Scottish football, challenging for trophies year after year and also playing regularly in in Europe. Uh and I think we're right to have that ambition, but to achieve it sustainably and consistently, we've got to strengthen the football operation on an ongoing basis. And that means recruiting well, developing players, building a successful player trading model, and creating a a pathway for our own young talent. We also want to build on the the success, the great progress we've had uh on the women's side. Our partnership with Jamestown Analytics is a is a really important part of all of that and I think will help us to make better informed decisions as we as we go forward. But clearly uh we've also got to keep growing the club commercially so that we have the resources to support our ambitions over the over the longer term. I think there's a big opportunity there as well. So there's a lot of work ahead but our goal is clear success on the pitch and a football club that our supporters and community can be proud of. When you look back over the last year, then how do you assess the the progress across the board at the club? Well, I would say there's been a lot of progress, but we also know that there's still plenty to do. Uh the first team went very close last season. The way it ended was uh it was really disappointing, especially after everything the players and staff had put into it. I think they deserved a better outcome, but we should recognize and pay tribute to them for what they did achieve, which was was actually exceptional. Our women's team also made history with a brilliant league championship win and our young players of course lifted the the Scottish Youth Cup. So, these are both very significant achievements in their in their own right. There's also been great progress on the on the business side. Um, and that's geared towards supporting what we what we want to achieve on the pitch. But all of that showed to me the considerable potential of the club and the strong foundations that we have to build on. The the task ahead of us is to turn that potential into success over the longer term. There was understandable frustration among our supporters after the way that last season ended and about the relative silence from the club afterwards. Can you explain some of the things that were happening behind the scenes over the summer? Well, the final week was was difficult on on a number of fronts. Uh, amongst other things, we were disappointed by the unprecedented decision that is the team uh leading the league uh at the time of the split. We had to play our final game away from home and obviously the circumstances at the end of that game were from our perspective completely unacceptable. We took advice and we made our concerns very clear to the to the football authorities. Standing back from it all, I think we'd like to see greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in in Scottish football because standards and processes matter, particularly at uh important points in the season, and I think there's room for for improvement. I understand the frustration about how little supporters heard from us afterwards. There was and and remains a live police investigation uh into into actions against our players uh and that uh obviously limited what we could say publicly. But I think even with those constraints, I think we could have communicated more more clearly. In the end, we had to think about what was best for hearts. With a new management team coming in, uh, a new season to prepare for, we felt the right thing for us was to draw a line and look forward. But our supporters should know that we did everything we could to stand up for hearts. We will always do that. Uh, and we certainly haven't forgotten what happened last season. But our focus now has to be on putting the club in the strongest possible position for this season and beyond and of course communicating better uh along the way. Staying with the the present day then how do you feel about where hearts are at the moment? Well, I think there's a lot to be positive about uh you know I think router and his staff have had a really significant impact and we're all extremely happy to have them at the club. Uh there's also uh excellent work taking place right across the football department under the the leadership of Graeme Jones. There's been a lot of change of course and we're still working through that and injuries and a demanding schedule have compounded the the challenge in some respects. Uh this feels to me certainly like a year of transition and there certainly been a few bumps along the way. That said, there's a huge amount to play for. We know there are areas where we want to do better and actually what matters most of all I think is that we keep improving year by year and we give the players and staff the support that they that they need to succeed. I've been really encouraged by what I've seen in the pitch and in the training ground. We have a a really good squad, some some great players. Uh I'm also very excited uh about the opportunity that that lies ahead for us uh and beyond this season. But we won't get carried away because as everyone knows, football has a a habit of bringing you back down to earth pretty pretty quickly. On matters off the field, we are currently recruiting for a new chief executive. What are some of the things that you're looking for for that potential candidate? Well, before talking about the candidate and the the appointment, I'd like to thank Andrew again for his contribution uh during his time at hearts and to wish him all the all the best for the future. We're making progress uh with the recruitment process. We've appointed an executive an executive search firm to help us find the right person and there are some very strong candidates in the process. We're looking for someone who understands the scale and and potential of hearts and shares our ambition. someone with the commercial uh strategic organizational uh leadership skills to help us take the club through its next uh phase of of development and it's an important appointment. Uh we want to get it right. In the meantime, we're fortunate to have a very strong executive team led by Cat McCllum, Yun Forbes, and Graeme Jones. And that means we're in the fortunate position of being able to take our time. The club's accounts will shortly be published. What can you say about the the current financial position of the club? Well, I don't want to preempt accounts, but I do want to take this opportunity to give supporters some context uh for the accounts. They will show a loss for the year. uh as expected. One factor was the absence of European income uh during a period when we were continuing to invest significantly in the in the playing squad and across the club. That uh investment was deliberate. It was intentional and the funding was in there uh was in place rather to uh to support it. But uh we also understand the the importance of maintaining strong financial discipline as we look to grow our income and and manage our spending uh in a responsible way. Overall uh you know I think the club's in a positive position. Our return to European football this season gives us uh uh more to build on but we'll explain the the figures and the wider financial picture in more detail when the accounts are published. We've spoken about the positive ambitions that we've got for the future. Does that require further investment then in your opinion? Well, we've been exploring further investment uh in order to give hearts greater financial strength and support the club's development. Um we've had some discussions and and those discussions are going well. uh I don't want to get ahead of them today but if they do conclude successfully that would be another positive step for hearts and would strengthen our ability to uh invest for the for the longer term but I think any uh investment has to be used sensibly the purpose would be to build a stronger football club fundamentally and to ensure that we have the resources in place to pursue our ambitions uh in the in the longer term At the same time, we are continuing to develop a player trading model which we expect to become an increasingly important contributor to the club's long-term financial sustainability. Finally then, Callum, after almost a year as chairman, what has struck you most about Harvey Football Club? Well, probably the scale of the club. Uh, I'm not sure you really appreciate that from the from the outside, but also just how much hearts means to so many people. I knew that as a supporter. Um, but you see it differently when you're involved uh every every day. You see the commitment of the staff and the the volunteers, the support the club receives from so many people and the special place it holds in their lives. You also quickly uh realize that whatever decision you make, somebody will tell you that you've got it wrong. But uh you know, I think that passion is part of what makes hearts special. The foundation of hearts is a huge part of that, too. So is the work of our charity partner, Big Hearts, and our connection with the with the wider community. All of that brings a real responsibility as we're looking after something that uh matters deeply to a lot of people. We are ambitious for the club. Uh I think there's a lot to be positive about and and optimistic about if all of us associated with Heart of Blotheian can pull in the in the same direction. And that's certainly what I would like to see us do while at the same time uh ensuring that we stay true to the the values that have defined our club for more than 150 years. Ken, thank you very much for your time. Thank you.

items.text: Hello, and welcome to Scarves Around the Funnel on the Whistle, brought to you in association with Trade Coach and Digital Soulway. It finished on Foundation Day at Tynecastle. And it feels like two dropped points against a bang average Rangers side who were bang average and went in by a goal to nil up after a first half in which Hearts had a lot of the ball, but very little threat at the other end of the pitch. Rangers were 1-0 up and Hearts won it 2-1 back then to continue their title push. Today, 1-0 down and a blisteringly quick start to the second half and scored two goals and unfortunately couldn't see it over the line. Um, a lot to get to. We'll keep it brief as always. It's all on the whistle. Our main episode will look back over the next 24 hours or so at events at Tynecastle in a bit more depth, but obviously all the talking points in the lead-up to this were to do with Derek McInnes'return to Tynecastle. Have to say, I didn't expect to see Cammy Devlin and Lawrence Shankland take their seats behind the dugouts. Sky intimated that would be the case in their coverage an hour before kickoff. And yeah, they got the reception that they deserved as did Derek McInnes. It was so close to to basically having the bragging rights on all three of them. But in the end, weirdly, somehow Rangers missed from like a yard out right at the death to to win the game. Honestly, there was a there's so much going on. Um, 25 home league games without defeat. And that was in jeopardy at halftime. That's now 26 home league games without defeat. It's the fifth draw and 21 wins. It brings to an end a run of 11 straight victories at Tynecastle in the league for Hearts. Two changes, Kingsley and Wilson, were replaced by Mandi and Miller. Good to see Loïc Mandi back from the start. He's had his minutes managed over the past two or three games, but deemed fit enough to start. And Calvin Miller playing in the number 10 role, which meant Stephen Kingsley was having his minutes managed, stayed on the bench to start with. Rogers Mato stayed at left-back like he did against Trabzonspor. Well, he stayed at full-back. He obviously switched back over from right-back. But Calvin Miller playing in the number 10 position and Saba Kums Jota keeping his place on the right-hand side of midfield. I thought we were really good the first 10 minutes um without really posing too many problems for Pandur, but we took the game to Rangers. They've got two or three pretty talented individuals, but I don't know if they didn't fancy the battle at the start or or what happened um because they didn't give those individuals that are much better than the other individuals much of the ball. And I thought we started well, uh controlled the game, but the goal we lost is so sloppy. You might get away with that in the fifth tier of English football if you're Loïc Mandi, but he's cost us a few goals this season. He was a part-time footballer a few years ago and a kitchen porter. So, to expect him to to be this kind of superstar, but he's got to learn and he's got to have learned by now. And it was Altona, who I thought was good today. Um, he played at right back. He plays it into Mandi, and it shouldn't be too difficult to get it back to McCart, but I don't know what he's doing. It was a sloppy touch, whether it was a pass or whatever it was. Uh, Kelsey plays a one-two with with Nadiri. Um, Thomas Magnusson's kind of unable to make the tackle. Nadiri shields it. And Kelsey shields it even better from Magnusson and fires through the legs of of Boruc. It was hard to take. Because it was it was two average sides, to be fair, in the first 20, 25 minutes. And they didn't have to work hard for the goal, and I don't like it when that happens. You want the opposition to have to work hard for their goal, like Trabzonspor scoring a good second goal against Hearts. We can't gift trap teams, and we've spoken a lot about the quality of the the opposition depends on how clinical they usually are in front of goal. He's a good striker. He's a decent striker, Kevin Kelsey, the Venezuelan. He's done all right over here in Major League Soccer. They spent a lot of money on him, and he wasn't missing from there. So, how we're going to react? How are we going to respond? Well, it was okay. Claudio Braga with the the effort from 16 yards after a quick throw. Uh, we were switched on with a quick throw. Little bit snappy with the shot, uh, Claudio Braga. And it I just felt in the first half it was a it was a combination of of things. We played some all right stuff. Um, we've done that quite a lot this season, kind of from about the half-hour mark towards half-time. We've we've really picked up, but the the first 10 minutes, um, apart up until probably the half hour mark. Um yeah, we we didn't really get into the game, but Rangers didn't really threaten. Uh decision-making was was poor. We had two or three long balls from McCart. The pressing was a bit bedraggled and it it just looked a bit disjointed in the first half cuz they were there for the taking, Rangers, um but we we couldn't find a way to to do so. Calvin Miller at the back post playing in that kind of central role, which I thought suited him today. That's certainly something that he can kind of come back and play as an eight and help out with the the two midfielders behind them or he can play as that 10 when when we've got the ball. I like that kind of hybrid role for Calvin Miller. His eighth of the season, that's a mistake initially by Min-kyu Kim. Bragason's driven shot, cross, whatever it was, deflected off Fernandez. How bad was he in the second half? And it falls to Calvin Miller who slots home and Hearts have turned it around within 12 minutes of the second half. They've gone from a goal down to 2-1 up. We knew that Rangers were going to uh we're going to push forward. We've got to be careful we don't get too deep in this game and invite them onto us. And every time we win the ball back, just hammer it clear. Anywhere will do. Cuz that's just a recipe for disaster. You've got to you've got to have some smarts. You've got to keep the ball when you got it. You've got to have runners making smart runs into areas into space. And there was there was a period of of play after we went 2-1 up. I was concerned that we were getting a bit too deep. Boy Nani had a shot saved after coming on as a sub. He had a shot saved in the 68th minute. We had a chance to put it out of sight. Claudio Bragga in the 76th minute. Brilliant bit of play again. We're switched on. We play it quick. And Bragga cuts all the way in uh and his shot is is saved. One thing I would say about this for anybody that that was at the game, there was a replay on Sky and I do think he might have been offside from the initial ball that's played to him over on the left-hand side in the first instance. Um again, it's immaterial now because he didn't score, but that would have been sore if that had been the the goal that put us 3-1 up and it ended up being chalked off for offside.
